Fungi: General introduction and characteristic features of phycomycetes, ascomycetes, basidiomycetes and deuteromycetes
Structure and reproduction of Mucor and Yeast

Algae: General introduction and characteristic features of green, brown and red algae; structure and reproduction of Spirogyra; economic importance of algae
Bryophyta: General introduction and characteristic features of liverworts, hornworts and moss; morphological structure and reproduction of Marchantia; economic importance of bryophytes

Gymnosperm: General introduction and characteristic features of Gymnosperms; morphology and reproduction of Pinus; economic importance of gymnosperm
Angiosperm: Morphology of root, stem, leaves, inflorescences, flowers and fruit
Taxonomic study: Definition, taxonomic hierarchy, classification systems (artificial, natural and phylogenetic) of angiosperms

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Basidiocarp.** The mushroom is the fleshy fruiting body of a basidiomycete, with a cap (pileus), stalk (stipe) and gills (lamellae) on which basidiospores are produced.  ·  **Edible mushrooms.** Agaricus bisporus (button mushroom) and Pleurotus (oyster mushroom) are cultivated widely and are rich in protein, vitamins and minerals.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Poisonous mushrooms.** Amanita muscaria (fly agaric) and other toxic species contain deadly toxins; misidentification can cause severe poisoning, so wild mushrooms must never be eaten unverified.  ·  **Ecological role.** Many mushrooms are decomposers, and forest trees depend on mycorrhizal fungal associations for mineral and water absorption.  ·  **Cultivation.** Mushroom farming uses composted substrate spawned with fungal mycelium under humid, shaded conditions — a growing cottage industry in Nepal.
